subject: Career
title: When Not to Send a Cover Letter
description: A short lesson to help you apply When Not to Send a Cover Letter.

hook.text: Sometimes the best cover letter is no cover letter. But how do you know when?

buildup.text: If the application explicitly says 'no cover letter,' respect the instruction. Follow directions.

discovery.text: In fast-moving tech, some hiring managers prefer a strong LinkedIn profile over a letter.

twist.text: But if the posting says 'optional,' it's not optional. Optional means 'we're testing who cares.'

climax.text: When in doubt, write one. The downside of skipping is bigger than the downside of sending.

quiz.question: What does 'cover letter optional' usually mean in a job posting?
options: It's a test — you should write one

details.summary: Some situations make cover letters unnecessary or even counterproductive: when the application explicitly says not to include one, when applying through referral channels, or when the online system provides no way to attach one. Wasting effort on an unread letter is poor strategy.
details.whyItMatters: Directing your effort where it creates the most impact is part of an effective job search. Knowing when a cover letter adds no value lets you focus time on higher-return activities.
takeaways: Skip cover letters when the job posting explicitly says not to include one
Referral applications often bypass the cover letter screening stage
Invest saved time in researching the company and tailoring your resume

faq.question: Should you write a cover letter if the job posting says it is optional?
faq.answer: Yes. Optional means it is a chance to differentiate yourself. Candidates who include a thoughtful cover letter when it is optional demonstrate initiative and genuine interest. The exception is if the company culture explicitly values brevity and directness over formal application materials.

faq.question: What should you do with the time saved by not writing a cover letter?
faq.answer: Invest it in researching the company for your interview, tailoring your resume more precisely, building a connection with someone at the company through networking, or applying the saved time to another high-priority application. Every hour should maximize your job search return.
